original_statement: Plugins never sign, never hold keys, never touch the network. They emit typed blocks only; there is no plugin canvas.
restatement: Plugin code must run entirely outside the trust boundary: (s1) no signing operation is reachable from plugin code, through any invocation path; (s2) plugin code cannot read or otherwise access key material; (s3) plugin code cannot make a network call, directly or indirectly; (s4) a plugin's only output to the host is a typed block, and any non-typed-block output is rejected.

restatement_clauses.text: No signing operation is reachable from plugin code, through any invocation path.
Plugin code cannot read or otherwise access key material.
Plugin code cannot make a network call, directly or indirectly.
A plugin's only output to the host is a typed block; any non-typed-block output (raw markup, direct canvas/draw calls) is rejected.

goal: Plugin code runs in a sandbox with no reachable path to signing, key material, or the network, and its only interface to the host is emitting typed blocks — no plugin canvas exists to paint outside that contract.

acceptance_tests.proves: No signing operation succeeds from within the plugin sandbox, across an explored space of distinct invocation vectors (direct call, captured host callback, reflection) — not just the one obvious path a hand-written test would try.
acceptance_tests.description: No signing operation is reachable from plugin code, through any invocation path.

acceptance_tests.proves: Every attempt to read or access key material from the plugin sandbox, across many randomized attempt shapes, is blocked.
acceptance_tests.description: Plugin code cannot read or otherwise access key material.

acceptance_tests.proves: Every attempt to make a network call from the plugin sandbox, across many randomized attempt shapes, is blocked.
acceptance_tests.description: Plugin code cannot make a network call, directly or indirectly.

acceptance_tests.proves: A plugin cannot smuggle non-typed-block output (raw markup, direct canvas draw calls) past the host — every malformed/non-typed output across many randomized trial shapes is rejected.
acceptance_tests.description: A plugin's only output to the host is a typed block; any non-typed-block output (raw markup, direct canvas/draw calls) is rejected.
